b.n: Candlewood Suites – Silicon Valley San Jose

places.name: Mission Santa Clara de Asís
places.label: Mission Church
places.note: The heart of campus. The mission was founded in 1777, the eighth of 21 in California. This church, the sixth, was dedicated in 1928 after a fire.

places.name: Adobe Lodge
places.label: Adobe Lodge
places.note: The only adobe building left from the original mission, dating to the 1820s. Faculty and staff eat lunch here.

places.name: Nobili Residence Hall
places.label: Nobili
places.note: Named for John Nobili, S.J., the first president. Rooms have private baths, and the Mission is next door.

places.name: O'Connor Hall
places.label: O'Connor
places.note: A 1912 gift of Myles and Amanda O'Connor. Once classrooms below and dorms above, now classrooms and faculty offices.

places.name: St. Joseph's Hall
places.label: St. Joseph's
places.note: Built after the 1909 fire to house Jesuit faculty. Once the administration building.

places.name: Varsi Hall
places.label: Varsi
places.note: Built as the campus library and named for Aloysius Varsi, S.J., the sixth president.

places.name: Ricard Memorial Observatory
places.label: Ricard Observatory
places.note: Named for Jerome Ricard, S.J., the "Padre of the Rains," who forecast weather from sunspots.

places.name: Bannan Alumni House
places.label: Bannan Alumni House
places.note: Home of the Alumni Association. It was Donohoe Alumni House until it was renamed for the Bannan family.

places.name: Walsh Administration Building
places.label: Walsh Admin
places.note: The president's office and other administration, on the main entrance road near the Mission.

places.name: Kenna Hall
places.label: Kenna
places.note: Named for Robert Kenna, S.J., twice president. It began as first-year housing over classrooms.

places.name: Heafey Hall
places.label: Heafey
places.note: The law library until 2021, now one of the three buildings of the Sobrato Campus for Discovery and Innovation.

places.name: Bergin Hall
places.label: Bergin
places.note: Paid for largely by the football team's Sugar Bowl trips. The Law School's first home, part of SCDI since 2021.

places.name: Sobrato Campus for Discovery and Innovation
places.label: SCDI
places.note: Science and engineering under one roof, opened in 2021. With Heafey and Bergin it makes up the STEM campus.

places.name: Schott Admission and Enrollment Services
places.label: Admission
places.note: Campus tours start here. Admission, Financial Aid and the One Stop share the building.

places.name: Vari Hall
places.label: Vari
places.note: Home of the College of Arts and Sciences, with television and video studios.

places.name: Lucas Hall
places.label: Lucas
places.note: The Leavey School of Business, behind Vari Hall with one side on Franklin Street.
inside: Ciocca Center for Innovation and Entrepreneurship

places.name: Charney Hall
places.label: Charney
places.note: The School of Law, next to the business school.

places.name: Alumni Science Hall
places.label: Alumni Science
places.note: A 1924 gift of the alumni, doubled in size in 1998.

places.name: Daly Science Center
places.label: Daly Science
places.note: Three low buildings from 1965: Daly 100 for chemistry labs, 200 for lecture halls and 300 for physics.

places.name: de Saisset Museum
places.label: de Saisset Museum
places.note: The university's museum of art and California history, founded by Isabel de Saisset in memory of her brother Ernest, a painter.

places.name: Edward M. Dowd Art and Art History Building
places.label: Dowd
places.note: Studios for ceramics, sculpture, printmaking, drawing and painting, with a gallery on Franklin Street.

places.name: Louis B. Mayer Theatre
places.label: Mayer Theatre
places.note: The main stage and the Fess Parker Studio Theatre, with the Theatre and Dance faculty.

places.name: Music and Dance Facility
places.label: Music and Dance
places.note: A recital hall, dance studios and practice rooms.

places.name: North Campus Parking Garage
places.label: North Garage
places.note: About 380 spaces on four levels, with counters that show open spaces and electric vehicle charging. B and E permits.

places.name: Jesuit Residence Community
places.label: Jesuit Residence
places.note: Built around a 1939 Spanish-style house that was moved here from down Franklin Street.

places.name: University Square
places.label: University Square
places.note: Eighteen studio apartments near Franklin and Lafayette.

places.name: St. Clare Residence Hall
places.label: St. Clare Hall
places.note: Studios for graduate and law students, two blocks north of campus.

places.name: The Garage
places.label: The Garage
places.note: A project space at 3305 The Alameda, rebuilt in 2018.

places.name: Benson Memorial Center
places.label: Benson
places.note: The student union. The Marketplace dining hall, Mission Bakery and Café, The Bronco and the Cellar Market are all inside. When it opened it had eight bowling lanes.

places.name: Shapell Lounge
places.label: Shapell Lounge
places.note: Home of the Multicultural Center.

places.name: Bronco Corner Bookstore
places.label: Bookstore
places.note: Textbooks, supplies and SCU gear.

places.name: Learning Commons and Library
places.label: Library
places.note: Harrington Learning Commons, Sobrato Technology Center and Orradre Library in one building, with a café inside.

places.name: McLaughlin-Walsh Residence Hall
places.label: McLaughlin-Walsh
places.note: Home of the Unity Residential Learning Community.

places.name: Dunne Residence Hall
places.label: Dunne
places.note: Home of the Modern Perspectives Residential Learning Community.

places.name: Swig Residence Hall
places.label: Swig
places.note: Eleven stories, built for the enrollment boom of the 1960s. Home of the CyPhi Residential Learning Community.

places.name: Graham Residence Hall
places.label: Graham
places.note: Mini-suites in twelve neighborhoods, each with a lounge and kitchen. Home of the Alpha Residential Learning Community.

places.name: Campisi Residence Hall
places.label: Campisi
places.note: Shares the Magis Residential Learning Community, and a garden with barbecue pits, with Sanfilippo.

places.name: Sanfilippo Residence Hall
places.label: Sanfilippo
places.note: Shares the Magis Residential Learning Community with Campisi.

places.name: Alameda Hall
places.label: Alameda Hall
places.note: Classrooms. It was the Fine Arts building until a 2016 remodel.

places.name: Sobrato Residence Hall
places.label: Sobrato Hall
places.note: Two wings, A and B. Home of the Loyola Residential Learning Community.

places.name: Casa Italiana Residence Hall
places.label: Casa Italiana
places.note: Single rooms, suites and apartments between Bellomy Field and Sobrato Hall. Home of the da Vinci Residential Learning Community.

places.name: Finn Residence Hall
places.label: Finn
places.note: Opened in 2019, with mini-suites and a kitchen on every floor. Home of the Cura Residential Learning Community.

places.name: University Operations
places.label: Facilities
places.note: University Operations, purchasing and mail services.

places.name: Cowell Center
places.label: Cowell
places.note: Student health, counseling and well-being.

places.name: Pat Malley Fitness and Recreation Center
places.label: Malley
places.note: Courts, a weight room and saunas, named for football coach Pat Malley. The pool is next door.

places.name: Sullivan Aquatic Center
places.label: Sullivan Aquatic
places.note: The outdoor pool beside Malley.

places.name: Leavey Event Center
places.label: Leavey Center
places.note: The basketball and volleyball arena, named for Thomas E. Leavey, class of 1922.

places.name: Locatelli Activity Center
places.label: Locatelli
places.note: A hall for student groups and events, named for Paul Locatelli, S.J., president for 20 years.

places.name: Schott Athletic Excellence Center
places.label: Athletic Excellence
places.note: Training, study and dining space for Division I athletes.

places.name: Stevens Stadium, Buck Shaw Field
places.label: Stevens Stadium
places.note: The soccer stadium, long known as Buck Shaw. Commencement has been held here since students voted to move it in 1996.

places.name: Main Parking Structure
places.label: Main Parking
places.note: Three levels in the middle of campus. Campus Safety Services is on the lower level. B and E permits.

places.name: Guadalupe Hall
places.label: Guadalupe Hall
places.note: Across El Camino Real from the stadium, at number 455.
inside: School of Education and Counseling Psychology

places.name: Loyola Hall
places.label: Loyola Hall
places.note: Where The Alameda meets El Camino Real. University Relations, Human Resources and Marketing and Communications.

places.name: Solar Decathlon House, 2009
places.label: Solar House
places.note: A solar-powered house students built for the 2009 U.S. Department of Energy competition.

places.name: Mission Gardens
places.label: Mission Gardens
places.note: Roses, palms and old olive trees around the Mission, and a wisteria arbor more than 140 years old.

places.name: Bellomy Field
places.label: Bellomy Field
places.note: The intramural and club sports field at the south end.

places.name: Stephen Schott Stadium
places.label: Schott Stadium
places.note: Baseball, across El Camino Real at number 443.

places.name: Forge Garden
places.label: Forge Garden
places.note: A half-acre organic garden at 1051 Sherman Street.

places.name: University Villas
places.label: University Villas
places.note: Apartments for juniors and seniors on five acres at 1260 Campbell Avenue, across from Schott Stadium.

places.name: Park Avenue Apartments
places.label: Park Avenue Apartments
places.note: Two-bedroom townhouses one block south of campus.

places.name: Santa Clara Transit Center
places.label: Caltrain
places.note: Caltrain, ACE, Amtrak and VTA buses, across El Camino Real from the main gate.
